name: Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree)
definition: A data structure storing partial sums to allow O(log n) updates and prefix-sum queries. A 'Half-tree' variant stores only half the nodes because prefix-sum queries starting from index 0 never require the right child of any node.
summary: The Fenwick Tree is a compact data structure storing partial sums for efficient point updates and prefix-sum queries, distinguished by its reduced memory footprint of 1.5n elements compared to standard binary trees.
